question: Which of the following materials is preferably used for electrical transmission lines?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** is a metal with** high conductivity** and **low resistance**, which makes it the **most preferred material** for **electrical transmission lines.**
 
• It is also used in **electrical wiring, motors, transformers**, and other electrical applications.
 
• Copper is a **good conductor of heat** and has **high corrosion resistance**, making it a durable material for long-term use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nichrome **is an alloy of **nickel and chromium**, which is known for its **high electrical resistance.**

 
 
• It is commonly used in** heating elements,** but not preferred for electrical transmission lines due to its **high resistance**.
 
• Nichrome wires are used in applications where heat resistance is required, such as i**n toasters, hair dryers, and ovens.**
 
 
 
• **Tungsten** is a metal with the** highest melting point **and **highest tensile strength** of all metals.
 
 
• It is commonly used in** filaments for incandescent light bulbs**, but not preferred for **electrical transmission lines** due to its** high cost and low conductivity.**
 
• Tungsten wires are used in applications where high temperature resistance is required, such as in **welding electrodes and rocket nozzles.**
 
 
 
• **Tin-lead alloy** is a mixture of tin and lead, which is commonly used as a **solder for electronic components.**
 
 
• It is not preferred for electrical transmission lines due to its **low conductivity and toxicity of lead**.
 
• Tin-lead alloys are used in applications where **low melting point **and** good wetting properties** are required, such as in electronic circuit boards.
